name: Oily Scalp
description: An oily scalp is characterized by an overproduction of sebum, leading to a shiny appearance and greasy feeling on the scalp. This can result in a sticky or dull texture on the hair, making it prone to buildup.
hair_texture: Shiny with possible stickiness or dullness
washing_frequency: Daily or every other day, depending on scalp condition
oil_recommendation: Use lightweight, non-greasy oils like argan or rosehip oil for occasional use only.

morning_routine.action: Wash the hair with a clarifying shampoo if needed

night_routine.action: Rinse thoroughly to remove any shampoo residue
night_routine.purpose: Prevent accumulation of product on the scalp overnight

weekly_care: Use a deep conditioning treatment once a week to replenish moisture without overwhelming the scalp.
heat_styling_recommendation: Limit heat styling and use heat protectants when needed.
foods_for_healthy_hair: Fatty acids from fish, nuts, and seeds
Vitamin E from avocados, almonds, and sunflower seeds
common_mistakes: Using heavy products that can weigh down the scalp
Neglecting to use a heat protectant when styling with heat tools
dont: Avoid leaving product on overnight unless instructed by your dermatologist or trichologist.
Do not over-wash as it can lead to dryness and irritation.

seasonal_care.summer: Stay hydrated and use lighter products to avoid excess oiliness
seasonal_care.winter: Be mindful of cold weather conditions which can exacerbate dryness; use moisturizing treatments if needed
seasonal_care.monsoon: Keep hair clean but avoid overwashing due to increased humidity.

expert_tips: Regular scalp massages can help improve circulation and reduce oiliness.
Use a fine-toothed comb or fingers instead of a brush to minimize breakage.
